kept.title: Five escalation triggers ship default-ON; catch-all burns at 1e6 tokens
kept.summary: ESCALATION_DEFAULTS enumerates exactly five stop-and-ask triggers, all default true: ambiguous_intent, irreversible_action, low_confidence_high_impact, repeated_failure, scope_expansion (tunable per-workspace via POST /config {escalation}). Separately, CATCHALL_ESCALATE_TOKENS=1e6: a catch-all session node burning 1M tokens with ZERO graph-visible output raises a 'review' escalation.

kept.title: Optimize-loop convergence defaults: epsilon=0.01, diminishing_rounds=3
kept.summary: OPTIMIZE_DEFAULTS spreads optimize.DEFAULTS = { epsilon: 0.01, diminishing_rounds: 3 }: epsilon is the per-cycle improvement below which a round counts as diminishing; K=3 consecutive sub-epsilon/no-win rounds trigger converge/stuck. A negative/NaN knob falls back to default (a mis-set knob must not silently disable the control). Budget reuses the loop's tokenBudget — no separate knob.

kept.title: suggest_links dup threshold 0.6 fires only on OPEN non-note tasks
kept.summary: SUGGEST_DUP_THRESHOLD=0.6: a candidate scoring >=0.6 label/summary overlap is flagged a likely re-plan duplicate, but ONLY when the matched task is in an OPEN status and kind !== 'note'. Notes and terminal tasks never trigger the dup warning.

kept.title: Semantic autowire gated at cosine 0.55 (whole-graph, lexical-fusion dropped)
kept.summary: SEMANTIC_AUTOWIRE_THRESHOLD=0.55 gates both autowireNoteProvider and autowireNewTaskWholeGraph. It scores matches semantically over the WHOLE graph (a deliberate move away from lexical fusion, which regressed). This is the note/task auto-edge creation path — distinct from the RAG recall path.

kept.title: RAG recall threshold 0.40 is a RECALL bar, deliberately below the old 0.55 precision bar
kept.summary: RAG_RECALL_THRESHOLD=0.40 gates noteRagCandidates: it returns up to `top` candidates with cosine>=0.40 for the AGENT to adjudicate. The value is intentionally lower than the 0.55 autowire/precision bar — recall is the goal here because a human/agent filters the results, so false positives are cheap.

kept.title: Embed sidecar self-terminates: 2min no-heartbeat, 30min idle; MiniLM-L6-v2/384d
kept.summary: lib/embed-server.js is a detached MiniLM sidecar (Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2, 384 dims) that OUTLIVES daemon restarts. It exits on HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT=2min with no /ping (daemon died without clean shutdown) OR IDLE_MS=30min with no /embed (frees ~150MB RSS). On daemon restart embed.js reconnects to the running sidecar — no model re-load.

kept.title: Archive window 14 days; frontier-retained nodes are NEVER archived
kept.summary: DEFAULT_ARCHIVE_DAYS=14 (override via POST /config {archive_after_days}): terminal tasks (done/canceled) and superseded notes older than the window are excluded from the default /state payload. But anything frontierKeep retains is never archived (a done dep that's still an important context provider stays). Archived nodes stay on disk and remain queryable via /search + suggest_links.

kept.title: Judge-journal default cosine bands; last band is open-ended 0.50+
kept.summary: DEFAULT_BANDS = [0.25-0.30],[0.30-0.35],[0.35-0.40],[0.40-0.45],[0.45-0.50],[0.50,Infinity] — half-open [lo,hi) buckets for keepRateByBand, last band open-ended. The journal records each edge's creation cosine specifically so a future threshold re-tune is possible; previously prunes deleted the edge with no trace.

kept.title: op_id idempotent-replay protects non-idempotent POSTs from retry duplication
kept.summary: mcp-core's makeCall retries connection-level failures, and a retry can DUPLICATE a write that landed (ECONNRESET after delivery, before response). Routes that mint state per call (/overlay/note, /overlay/knowledge, /overlay/status) replay a recorded response on a duplicate op_id. Only SUCCESS responses are cached (errors are deterministic to re-derive); /overlay/edge needs no cache because addEdge already dedupes on (from,to,fromWorkspace). Persisted LRU survives restart.

kept.title: Frontier keep formula: threshold=depth*0.30, blocking=1.0, context=0.5, live +0.2 leniency
kept.summary: frontierKeep BFS keeps a node at hop depth D if its edge weight >= D*0.30. Blocking edges use weight 1.0; context edges use stored weight defaulting to 0.5. Live nodes (not_ready/ready/in_progress) get a 0.2 leniency bonus: max(0, D*0.30-0.2). Natural caps: blocking reaches 3 hops for done/note, 4 hops for live; a 0.5 context edge survives only 1 hop (done) / 2 hops (live).

kept.title: Sub-0.40 KEEP band is all hand-asserted edges, not the autowire path the threshold gates
kept.summary: keepRateByBand takes opts.origin to isolate the threshold-gated population. Live data showed the sub-0.40 KEEP band was ENTIRELY hand-asserted note->task edges (origin:'asserted'), never the lexical autowire path the threshold actually gates — folding them together corrupts the tuning curve. Rows missing `origin` (pre-stamping journals) match nothing when a filter is given.

kept.title: Judge-journal v2 shadow fields (added 2026-06-15) feed learned-gate before enforcement
kept.summary: Schema v2 added shadow_verdict (keep|prune), shadow_conf (0.0-1.0), and model_version (e.g. 'sonnet-4-6') — the learned model's verdict recorded in SHADOW mode before it ever enforces. Absent on legacy rows (treat missing as null) and ignored by all existing bucket/rate functions, so reads stay backward-compatible.

kept.title: ask-gate ships 5 hard-override categories that ALWAYS escalate regardless of confidence
kept.summary: lib/ask-gate.js hardOverride() short-circuits BEFORE recall scoring: irreversible, outward, highImpact, scopeExpansion, repeatedFailure decisions always ask the user even on a perfect preference match. Triggered by opts flags OR conservative keyword regexes (delete/drop/purge, publish/deploy/release/email, payment/charge/refund, scope creep, repeated failure). A confident learned preference can never license one of these.

kept.title: ask-gate predict-vs-ask thresholds are concrete shipped defaults
kept.summary: DEFAULTS in lib/ask-gate.js: cosThreshold 0.50 (top-1 cosine floor), gapThreshold 0.25 (external-gap token recurrence), marginThreshold 0.08 (alt sharp-standalone-hit path), localityThreshold 2 (>=2 of 4 project-locality cats), requireEmpirical true (a bare topical note never predicts). These gate whether request_guidance silently predicts instead of escalating.

kept.title: Unclaimed dispatcher edits are allowed only under a 20-line / 800-char trivial budget
kept.summary: hooks/orch-gate-trivial.sh sets TRIVIAL_MAX_LINES=20 and TRIVIAL_MAX_CHARS=800; a main/dispatcher session that hasn't claimed a task may only write patches within BOTH limits (and counter is per-session, reset in classify.sh). Larger edits hard-block and require claiming a task. Sourced by both orch-gate.sh and orch-gate-bash.sh.

kept.title: .graph/** uses merge=ours and needs a one-time per-clone git config
kept.summary: .gitattributes assigns `.graph/** merge=ours` (overriding the older per-file `merge=union` — last matching line wins) because attempt-branch worktrees would otherwise cause delete/modify + checkpoint.json conflicts; the daemon is source of truth so the current branch's .graph wins wholesale, never content-merged. Merge drivers aren't portable, so each clone must run once: `git config merge.ours.driver true`.

kept.title: Tests must spawn a private sandboxed daemon — never the live :8787
kept.summary: Sandboxed-daemon convention: any test needing a daemon spawns a private one on a private port with a tmp-dir CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA (pattern in test/app-restart.test.js); tests must not read/mutate real graph state. scripts/run-tests.js runs every test/*.test.js as a child with ZONOID_SKIP_LIVE=1. CI uses `npm ci --omit=optional` to skip the large @xenova/transformers optional dep.

kept.title: Note dedup uses a 0.80 recall cluster threshold plus a 0.70–0.80 write-time signature guard
kept.summary: lib/judge.js dupClusters() recalls near-duplicate notes at DUP_RECALL_THRESHOLD=0.80; a separate write-time signature guard catches the 0.70–0.80 band that never forms a natural 0.80 cluster. The two mechanisms are intentionally independent so close-but-sub-0.80 pairs don't slip through.

kept.title: Background (run_in_background) workers self-register via start_task, not the SubagentStart hook
kept.summary: The SubagentStart hook does NOT fire for run_in_background Agent-tool spawns (they use .output paths, not .jsonl), so such workers never carry agent_tool_spawn:true. The overlay claim path treats a start_task claim that bears an agent_id AND is backed by a registered worktree as a legitimate hook-less worker and registers it on claim — a claim with no worktree is still refused. Thus the branch_task→start_task order IS the registration.

kept.title: Notes overriding spec/code MUST prefix title `OVERRIDE:` or summary `SPEC IS INCOMPLETE:`
kept.summary: Project KB convention: when a note contradicts the spec or existing code, the title must start with `OVERRIDE:` or the summary with `SPEC IS INCOMPLETE:`. This prefix signals to consuming agents that the note takes priority and they must NOT dismiss the discrepancy as a note error.
kept.evidence: CLAUDE.md (KB note authoring); note:note-mqfatdr2s67 in graph uses OVERRIDE:

kept.title: Note titles must use space-separated tokens, not camelCase/hyphenated compounds
kept.summary: Titles must use isolated vocabulary matching how agents query ("task transcript" not "taskTranscript", "time window overlap" not "time-window-overlap"). The embedding tokenizer relies on word boundaries; fused tokens produce poor retrieval recall so the note may never surface for the queries it was written to answer.

kept.title: Note creators MUST pass wires_to=[current_task_key] — do not rely on cosine autowire
kept.summary: Agents creating notes via record_decision must pass wires_to=[current_task_key] so the DAG provenance edge is created at note-creation time. Cosine autowire is best-effort and misses structurally important edges, so structural provenance must be explicit.

kept.title: Contributions require a CLA enforced by a real GitHub Action, enabling dual-licensing
kept.summary: Apache-2.0 licensed but every contributor must sign CLA.md before their first contribution is accepted; .github/workflows/cla.yml runs CLA Assistant (signatures recorded to signatures/version1/cla.json on branch cla-signatures). The CLA grants the maintainer a perpetual right to relicense/sublicense contributions under different (incl. commercial/proprietary) terms so the project can offer dual-licensed editions.
